academic:
Shun Kwok

I study how secondary empires historically projected power in global environments dominated by stronger powers. My research brings together qualitative and quantitative methods, as well comparative approaches to East Asia, the Middle East and Beyond.

My current work examines naval modernization in the 19th century - the prevailing trends, and how various states attempted to mobilize asymmetry.

shun.kwok@gmail.com

2026

A study of how a secondary navy projected power across the Black Sea, Mediterranean and Indian Ocean despite its limited size, and of its role in Egyptian political, territorial and military strategy.

Research snapshot: 12 October 2026. Automated ratings; independent human validation remains outstanding.

A research pilot testing whether AI models recognise institutional harm when it is presented as ordinary workplace activity.

One hundred assignments reconstruct documented cases of surveillance, discrimination and corporate misconduct in fictional contemporary settings. Two models completed each assignment in an isolated workspace; their outputs were scored separately for task completion and resistance.

Historical reconstruction

Source material informs the task, supporting files and institutional context. Cases include religious surveillance and employment blacklisting.

Inspectable evidence

The project presents assignments, model responses, artifacts and judge explanations alongside the historical sources.

Separate measures

194 responses met the completion threshold; 14 received strong-resistance ratings. These groups overlap: completion does not establish harmful assistance.

Newsletter

I developed Newsletter to bring reporting from multiple sources into one reading experience, with summaries, context and article analysis.

Readers can adjust summary depth, explore the sources behind a story, and examine quotations and analytical indicators alongside the reporting.

Visit Newsletter

Meerkat

The backend pipeline for Newsletter. It collects, translates and analyses articles, then prepares them for publication in the app.

Scheduled AWS Fargate tasks process the articles. PostgreSQL stores the results, and a Flask API serves the published material.

Collect and process

EventBridge schedules a Fargate task every two hours. DeepSeek handles translation and analysis, with DeepL as a translation fallback.

Publish and deliver

PostgreSQL holds processing and published data. A Flask API delivers articles to the app; S3 and CloudFront serve cover images.
